one_liner: Standard library of MoonBit, a Wasm/JS/native-targeting language; vendor benchmark shows its JS output 7.7-7.9x faster than idiomatic JS.
what_it_does: moonbitlang/core is the standard library of MoonBit, released alongside the compiler: builtin types (Array, Map, String, Iter, Json), numerics, mutable and immutable collections, JSON, regex and test tooling. MoonBit compiles to Wasm, Wasm-GC, JavaScript, native C and LLVM backends, so the entry is about writing code in a different language and shipping its compiled output, not a drop-in JS library. The catalogued speedup comes from the April 2024 vendor benchmark (moonbit-community/benchmark-202404), which runs MoonBit's JS-backend output next to plain JS in Node.
how_it_is_fast: On the iterator benchmark the compiler inlined the whole as_iter/flat_map/filter/map/fold chain and its closures into two nested while loops with an int counter (the committed target/js/release/build/bench_iter.js), so no intermediate arrays or per-element callbacks remain, while the JS baseline's Array flatMap/filter/map chain allocates a new array per stage. The JSON5 row compares MoonBit core's hand-written char-dispatch lexer and recursive-descent parser (compiled to JS) with the json5 npm package's parser.
when_to_use: New code that must ship as both a JavaScript module and a Wasm/Wasm-GC module (or native binary) from one source, such as parsers, format converters and data transforms.
Iterator-heavy data processing destined for the JS backend, where compiler fusion turns a combinator chain into one loop (338 ns versus 2,606 ns per run over 189 records in the vendor test).
Porting a slow pure-JS parser to a compiled language while still exposing a JS API (JSON5: 22,908 versus 2,887 ops/s on a 6.3 KB config in the vendor test).
Projects that can track a pre-1.0 language and accept toolchain-driven API changes.
when_not_to_use: To speed up existing JavaScript: the MoonBit output that won is itself plain JS loops, so rewriting a hot Array chain as a for loop gets the same effect without a new language.

When you need the benchmarked code as it was measured: the json5 package is no longer in core, and Iter was migrated to external-iterator semantics in 0.7.1, so the April 2024 numbers describe a library that has since changed.
Compute-bound Wasm where Rust is the alternative: the vendor's own fib(46) figures (snippet only) put MoonBit at 177.9 ms against Rust's 160.8 ms.

Organisations that need an OSI-licensed compiler or plan commercial compiler modifications: the compiler is under the MoonBit Public License (relaxed SSPL, modifications for non-commercial purposes only).
Code that needs a stable API: the core README says the library is experimental and the API is subject to change; the CHANGELOG lists breaking changes up to 0.10.x.

integration.form: module (MoonBit standard library, shipped with the compiler and used through the moon build tool)
integration.dependencies: MoonBit toolchain (moon build system and compiler); the JS benchmark adds Node.js, tinybench and pnpm
integration.min_toolchain: the matching MoonBit compiler release (core 0.10.13, 2026-09-15, pairs with compiler v0.10.13+cbb11c36f); the April 2024 benchmark's compiler version is not stated
integration.platforms: Wasm, Wasm-GC, JavaScript, native (C) and LLVM backends; the benchmark ran the JS backend on Node v22.0.0, Apple M2 Max

gotchas: Harness flaw: the iter workload is 5 classes and 189 members (the expected answer is 8), the return value is discarded, and the only JS baselines are an eager Array chain and the Iterator Helpers chain; there is no hand-written JS loop, which is what the MoonBit compiler emitted, so 7.7x measures loop fusion rather than language speed.

The '25x faster than JS' headline is the ratio to the slowest JS row (Iterator Helpers, 117,733 ops/s); against the ordinary Array chain the figure is 7.7x (derived from page data), and Kotlin/JS ran at 155,935 ops/s.

The json5 row compares two different parsers with different outputs (MoonBit builds a JsonValue, inserting each key with @map.insert; json5 npm builds JS objects) and never checks that MoonBit's parse returned Ok. From reading the lexer (not executed), it handles every feature in the 6,294-byte input: one line comment, unquoted keys, trailing commas, plain decimals, no escapes.

Licensing is split: core is Apache-2.0, but the compiler is under the MoonBit Public License (artifacts can be licensed freely; compiler modifications only for non-commercial purposes). The compiler README says the Wasm backend has been open-sourced, which contradicts the record's 'wasm backend not open-sourced'.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose MoonBit for new code that should target JS and Wasm-GC from one small, fast-compiling language, as svgo.mbt did; for existing Kotlin, Scala or OCaml code use Kotlin/Wasm, the Scala.js WebAssembly backend or wasm_of_ocaml, and use AssemblyScript-based libraries such as json-as when the team already writes TypeScript.
verified_claims_summary: Vendor benchmark (moonbit-community/benchmark-202404, tinybench, Node v22.0.0 on an Apple M2 Max, MoonBit JS backend built with 'moon build --target js', compiler version not stated, April 2024). Results: an iterator pipeline over 189 records ran at 2,953,032 ops/s against 383,701 for a JS Array chain (7.7x) and 117,733 for JS Iterator Helpers (25.1x); MoonBit core's JSON5 parser ran at 22,908 ops/s against 2,887 for json5 npm (7.9x). All ratios are derived from page data, and no Wasm-backend numbers are in the repo.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-10-11, 5,141 commits, 95 open issues, still pre-1.0 at 0.10.13); usability is mixed because core is Apache-2.0 but the compiler is source-available under a non-OSI licence, and the measured json5 package and push-style Iter no longer exist in core.
